**Test image observations:** Mango leaf with discrete, irregular brown/necrotic lesions scattered across the leaf surface. The spots have dark brown centers with defined edges, some with lighter halos. No white powdery coating, no sooty black coating, no tip dieback pattern. This pattern is classic for anthracnose — irregular dark necrotic spots on leaves.

Now let me view one reference image from the Anthracnose class to confirm.

**Analysis:**

The reference Anthracnose image shows extensive leaf browning/necrosis — somewhat different presentation, but still consistent with the disease class which varies in severity.

**Comparing test image to all classes:**
- **Anthracnose**: Discrete dark necrotic lesions scattered on leaf — matches the test image well (irregular brown spots with defined edges on a green leaf)
- **Die_Back**: Browning progressing from tip/margin inward — not seen in test image
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White powdery coating on leaf surface — absent in test image
- **Sooty_Mould**: Black sooty fungal coating — absent in test image

The test image shows multiple discrete irregular brown necrotic spots on an otherwise green leaf, which is characteristic of Anthracnose infection.
